description: This chapter deals with the various ways of arranging and selecting objects. In Permutations, the order is important, whereas in Combinations, only the selection matters.

sections.title: Fundamental Principle of Counting
sections.description: This principle helps in calculating the total number of ways events can occur without actual counting.

key_concepts.explanation: If task A can be done in 'm' different ways and following it, task B can be done in 'n' different ways, then the total ways both tasks can occur together is m * n.
If task A can be done in 'm' ways and task B in 'n' ways, but both cannot occur simultaneously (Mutually Exclusive), then the total ways either A or B can occur is m + n.

sections.title: Factorial Notation
sections.description: The continued product of the first 'n' natural numbers is called a factorial. It forms the basis of calculating permutations and combinations.

key_concepts.explanation: It is defined only for positive integers and zero. Factorials do not exist for negative numbers and fractions.

sections.title: Permutations
sections.description: Arranging a set of given objects in a definite order is called a permutation. Here, the position of objects matters.

results: The total number of ways to arrange r objects at a time from n distinct objects is nPr.
If out of n objects, p are identical objects of one kind and q are identical objects of another kind, then total permutations = n! / (p! * q!).
The number of ways to arrange r objects from n distinct objects, where each object can occur any number of times = n^r

sections.title: Combinations
sections.description: Selecting or grouping a set of given objects, where the order does not matter, is called a combination.

steps.title: Identify Total Objects
steps.detail: Determine the total number of available objects or options (n) given in the problem.

steps.title: Determine Objects to Select
steps.detail: Find the number of objects (r) that you need to select for the group.

steps.title: Apply Formula
steps.detail: Apply the combination formula nCr and get the answer by expanding the factorials.

sections.title: Circular Permutations
sections.description: The ways of arranging objects in a circle are called circular permutations. There is no specific starting or ending point.

cases.condition: Clockwise and Anti-clockwise arrangements are different
results: Example: Seating n persons around a round table.

cases.condition: Clockwise and Anti-clockwise arrangements are same
results: Example: Making a necklace from n beads or a garland from flowers.
